name: Lakeside Hideaway
tagline: A protected veranda on the weather side, with a solar roof.
description: A 40-foot container turned so its long side faces the lake, with a deep screened veranda, a solar roof and living space opened to the water. The veranda gives shade in summer and a sheltered edge in shoulder seasons.

zones.name: Sleeping
zones.accessibility: Lake-facing window; turning space needs an accessible variant.

solar.mounting: fixed tilt, due south; snow-shedding; roof structure and wind uplift need review
solar.source: SolarCalculator.CA Ottawa: 39° optimal fixed tilt; brief range 36–39° year-round, winter ~60°, summer ~30°, due south.
solar.note: True south; confirm magnetic declination, shading, snow shedding and structural fixing.

porches.note: Deep protected veranda facing the lake.

foundation.type: Engineered helical piles with adjustable brackets
foundation.frost_design: Engineered pile depth and uplift resistance below frost; geotechnical review required.
foundation.ground_disturbance: Point loads only; no slab, fill or grade change. Use matting, root protection and a construction sequence reviewed by an arborist.
foundation.note: Elevated floor on engineered helical piles. Confirm soil, bedrock, frost uplift, corrosion, lateral capacity, slope stability and permit requirements before construction.

features.outdoor: 6.0 × 3.0 m screened veranda plus 1.0 m deck
features.solar: Raised PV above an extensive green roof
features.green_roof: Solar roof; green roof not included; saturated weight and drainage need engineering
features.accessibility: Step-free veranda intended; bathroom is compact.
features.environment: Shading from the veranda and a green roof; lake edge must remain undisturbed.

materials.material: Reclaimed 40 ft / 20 ft ISO high-cube steel containers
materials.source: Documented salvage; inspect structure, coatings, prior cargo and floor treatment
materials.disclosure: Reuse avoids new steel but adds transport, reinforcement and insulation. Not automatically lower impact than timber.
Continuous external insulation reduces thermal bridging. Thickness and moisture performance need hygrothermal review.

materials.material: Reclaimed or certified timber battens and boards
materials.disclosure: Replaceable, repairable, but needs durable species, ventilation and fire review.

materials.material: Timber frame, decking, insect screen and steel connectors
materials.disclosure: Separate from the container envelope so it can be repaired or removed.

materials.material: Membrane, PV modules and optional extensive green roof
materials.disclosure: Green roofs add saturated weight and maintenance. PV output depends on orientation, shading and snow.

provenance.method: Original concept schema and geometry for Containers Hamlet Design Lab. Not a measured, engineered or permit-ready design.
provenance.verification: None. No architect, engineer, building official or accessibility consultant has reviewed this concept.

status: concept only; not reviewed; not for construction

licence.note: Editor source code is AGPL-3.0-or-later. Original concept documentation, diagrams and sample data are CC BY-SA 4.0.

trellises.note: Trellis at the living end of the veranda.

thermal.wall_insulation_strategy: continuous external wood-fibre board (180 mm) with thermal breaks and a ventilated rainscreen
thermal.air_vapour_control: exterior-insulated, vapour-open assembly; sealed interior air barrier (to be detailed)
thermal.window_performance: triple glazed, low-e, argon, thermally broken frames
thermal.notes: Conceptual thermal intent only. No energy or code calculation.
thermal.thermal_bridge_mitigation: continuous external insulation with thermal washers and stainless fasteners; breaks at openings, pile caps and service penetrations

envelope.thermal_breaks: continuous external insulation with thermal washers and stainless fasteners; breaks at openings, pile caps and service penetrations
envelope.air_vapour_control: exterior-insulated, vapour-open assembly with a sealed interior air barrier; joints and service penetrations to be detailed
envelope.fire: combustible insulation, cladding and cavity need a fire review; cavity barriers, cladding classification and separation are not resolved
envelope.fastening: long fasteners pass through the insulation into the steel frame; pull-out, corrosion, thermal bridging and water shedding need engineering review
envelope.penetrations: openings, cladding rails, planter brackets and service penetrations need structural and waterproofing review
envelope.maintenance: inspect cladding, sealant, cavity, fasteners and vegetation twice a year and after severe weather
envelope.notes: Wood fibre is vapour-open and renewable; it needs robust temporary weather protection and fire detailing.
